## Guide rules not applied (different project)
Voltage regulator and heat pad, RS-232/DE-9 connector parts and their 100 pF caps, metal enclosure fit and mounting-ring bonding, orthogonal-layer routing.

## Deliberate deviation
The guide advises against a solid layer and routing on both layers. Here B.Cu is a solid ground plane and signals live on F.Cu, because there are only six slow signals and the goal of the rule (a ground return under every trace) is met.

## Open items to check before ordering
1. Print `reports/print_1to1_letter.pdf` (or the A4 version) at Actual size (30 mm ruler included; it must measure 30 mm) and lay the ESP32 and CC1101 modules on it. This confirms row spacing (25.4 mm assumed) and the CC1101 header pitch (2.54 mm assumed; some modules use 1.27 mm).
2. Bill of materials: 2 × 1x15 2.54 mm header (ESP32 sockets), 1 × 2x4 2.54 mm header for the CC1101; optional: C1 470 µF 16 V radial electrolytic (D8 mm, 3.5 mm pitch), C3 22 µF 16 V radial electrolytic (D5 mm, 2 mm pitch), C2 and C4 100 nF X7R through-hole ceramic (5 mm pitch, 50 V).
3. Two decoupling pairs, each an electrolytic plus a 100 nF ceramic; populate only what is needed. VIN pair (left of the ESP32, VIN pin 15 to GND): C1 470 µF electrolytic (D8 mm, 3.5 mm pitch) and C2 100 nF ceramic (5 mm pitch). 3V3 pair (above the CC1101 header; C4 next to its VCC pin, C3 2.5 mm further up so it clears the module in rev B): C3 22 µF electrolytic (D5 mm, 2 mm pitch; anything from 10 to 47 µF works) and C4 100 nF ceramic. Electrolytic polarity: pad 1 (square) is the positive supply pad (VIN or 3V3). Fit C1 when powering from VIN through long wires or a battery; on USB power it isn't needed. 470 µF is well over the USB inrush limit (10 µF), which can occasionally upset a strict port or hub at plug-in; if fitted on USB anyway, 47–100 µF is a reasonable compromise.
4. Lay the CC1101 breakout on the 1:1 print with its header over J1. Check that it clears C4 above the header and C3 (rev B: its body should sit about 0.8 mm outside the module's edge), and that its antenna and any overhang suit the board edge. The breakout's own dimensions are not in this design.

## Placement
Board is 95 × 55 mm (8 mm extra on the left for the VIN capacitors, 5 mm extra on the right for the CC1101 breakout). ESP32 USB end is 1 mm in from the bottom edge. Ruler is 30 mm.

## Antenna keep-out
The top 9.2 mm of the board (above the ESP32 pin rows, the full width) has no ground pour on either layer and no vias. One signal, MOSI, still runs through this strip: GPIO23 is the top pin of the right-hand row (level with the strip), so its trace leaves the pad and runs about 22 mm east at 0.8 mm below the pin row. It is a 0.3 mm 3.3 V digital line; the effect on the antenna is expected to be small, but it is metal in the keep-out. To remove it, move MOSI to a lower pin on the right-hand row.

## Pin map
clk GPIO18, mosi GPIO23, miso GPIO19, cs GPIO22, gdo0 GPIO21, gdo2 GPIO4. None are strapping pins (GPIO0/2/5/12/15).

## Capacitor spacing (hand soldering)
Board is 95 × 55 mm (extra 5 mm on the CC1101 side for the breakout board). C1's body is 1.8 mm from the left board edge. C2 sits directly below the VIN trace (pad 1 on the trace), 2.75 mm from C1's body and 0.85 mm from the ESP32 module's silkscreen outline. C3 and C4 are 5 mm apart pad to pad horizontally; in rev B, C3 sits 2.5 mm higher than C4.
